done.why: I had the egg in the trophy case by turn 70 and was deep in the underground, in the Temple pocket with the platinum bar and sceptre, about to drop the sword for the torch and try praying at the altar, when the world told me I'd used all 150 turns. There was plenty left I hadn't seen: the troll room's south and west exits, the cellar crawlway, the north-south passage's northeast fork, the hole under the altar.

about: A trimmed-down version of Zork: a white house with a trophy case, a forest with one climbable tree holding a jewelled egg, and an underground that has been deliberately fenced off with signs from 'The Management' (canyon view, dam, reservoirs all closed) so that what's left is a compact loop of cellar, troll room, round room, loud room, chasm, and a dome-and-temple pocket you drop into by rope and can't climb back out of. It is about collecting treasures for the case, but the underground also keeps hinting at someone who was here before you: the sorted rubble, the practised axe scratches, the barred trap door.

ending.what: I did the thing I came for (egg in trophy case, 20 of 350 points, rank Beginner) but the game did not treat that as an ending, and I ran out of turns underground with more treasures in hand and no way home found yet.

moments.note: The trophy case has 'the patient air of something that expects to be filled.' Better than I expected from a piece of furniture.
Canyon View roped off by the Frobozz Magic Scenery Company. First sign the map has been trimmed on purpose.
No low branch to climb, 'which saves a good deal of argument.'

Forest wandering: four near-identical forest rooms with no climbable tree, storm-tossed trees, rank undergrowth. Took me 30 turns to find the one tree, which was on the path north of the house all along.
Grating locked from beneath. Clear enough that the way in is from below, but no idea yet where.
Found the egg, 'scavenged by a childless songbird.' The nest built by a bird 'with better taste in treasure than in architecture.'
Putting the egg in the trophy case just says 'Done.' After all that, I wanted a flourish; examining the case afterwards was nicer.
Trap door crashes shut and someone bars it. I'm locked underground. Who?
Killed the troll in one blow. Easier than I feared; black fog ate the body.
'Your load is too heavy' for the axe. The weight limit bit me again and again after this: torch, candles, coffin, torch again.
The cave-in rubble sorted into neat heaps 'as though its sorter had stepped out for a moment, some time ago.' Someone else is down here.
Loud Room echoes every command back. 'Leaflet leaflet ...' Took me a beat to realise the room was the obstacle.
The platinum bar, 'quite silent, which in this room is a distinction.'
Dam closed for inspection, then reservoir closed, then reservoir south closed. Three fences in a row from The Management; funny once, wearing by the third.
The game decides for me that I won't be the one to finish clearing the rubble. I'd rather be told why I can't than be told I've decided not to.
Rope down into the Torch Room, rope ending five feet above my head. I realised a turn later I'd just committed myself.
The hole under the altar: 'a great many people sighing a very long way off.'
Dropped the bottle, still too heavy for the torch. Inventory juggling was the main puzzle of the last 40 turns.
Turn cap hit mid-batch, just as I was about to try praying at the altar.

wished: Carry more, or at least be told what's heavy. 'Your load is too heavy' five times (turns 83, 123, 135, 141, 146) with no sense of how close I was.
Have a go at clearing the sorted rubble myself (turn 113), or be told why not, instead of 'you decide not to be the one who does.'
Find out who barred the trap door behind me (turn 74). It's the best hook in the game and nothing followed it in my 150 turns.
Some acknowledgement at the trophy case beyond 'Done.' (turn 70) when the egg goes in.
Get back up the rope from the Torch Room, or know before I went down that I couldn't.
A less same-looking forest: four 'Forest' rooms with identical tree descriptions made the search for the climbable tree feel like wandering rather than exploring (turns 29 to 46).
More turns. 150 was enough for the egg but not for a completionist underground.

lines.line: It has the patient air of something that expects to be filled.
lines.why: Set the tone: the furniture has opinions. Made me want to fill it.

lines.line: It is rather deeper than leaves usually lie, as though someone had swept them together on purpose.
lines.why: First hint that someone else has been arranging this place.

lines.line: ...wedged into the fork of a branch by a songbird with better taste in treasure than in architecture.
lines.why: Made me laugh out loud at the moment of getting the thing I came for.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: Turned a treasure hunt into being trapped. Who is down here with me?

lines.line: ...the rubble is sorted into neat heaps, smallest nearest, as though its sorter had stepped out for a moment, some time ago.
lines.why: Eerie and precise. The absent sorter stayed with me the rest of the game.

lines.line: It is cold to the touch, and quite silent, which in this room is a distinction.
lines.why: The best joke in the game, and it only works because of the Loud Room.

lines.line: The railing is very solid. It is the most reassuring thing you have seen in some time.
lines.why: Funny and true: I'd just been sealed underground and fenced off three times.

lines.line: ...a faint sound, like a great many people sighing a very long way off.
lines.why: Made the one-way hole genuinely unsettling. I wanted to go down it and didn't dare.

lines.line: Ramses II was buried in it, and has evidently been moved elsewhere since, which the face does not seem to know.
lines.why: A small sad joke in a gold coffin.

fun.why: Finding the egg, dropping the troll in one swing, discovering the Loud Room's trick and the rope drop into the dome were all real pleasures. The forest wander and the repeated weight limit dragged.

engagement.why: I never wanted to stop; the barred trap door and the sorted rubble kept me asking who else was down here, and I hit the turn cap mid-plan rather than running out of things to do.

difficulty.why: The egg itself was easy once I found the tree: climb, take, walk home, put in case. The troll died in one blow. The only real friction was the inventory limit and the forest maze, neither of which felt like a puzzle so much as a tax.

interestingness.why: The closed-off map is a clever conceit (signs from The Management), and the absent presence underground (sorter, barrer, axe-practiser) is a real thread. The forest and the by-the-numbers house are less interesting.

prose.why: Every new examine paid off with a dry, exact line: the silent platinum bar, the reassuring railing, the coffin's face, the sighing hole. The best writing I've met in a place like this.
